This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Toronto Pearson Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 31 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=cyyz

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent showers and embedded thunderstorms across Toronto on August 31 have reduced solar insolation and enhanced evaporative cooling, suppressing daytime heating and anchoring market-implied odds on a daily maximum near 20–22 °C. Official guidance from the Japan Meteorological Agency and multiple numerical weather prediction runs converge on a daytime maximum near 29–30°C under mostly cloudy skies, light northeasterly flow, and moderate humidity levels that limit strong surface heating. Recent late-August observations show daily highs stabilizing around 28–29°C amid persistent cloud cover and weak winds, consistent with the early-September climatological transition from peak summer warmth. 

These conditions reduce the likelihood of significant further warming or rapid cooling, keeping the distribution tightly centered on 28–30°C while assigning only modest probability to outliers. Traders are weighting the consensus of short-range model guidance and the absence of disruptive synoptic features—such as stronger onshore flow or clearing skies—that could shift the outcome outside this narrow band.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models and recent observations position 32–33°C as the most likely peak temperatures for Singapore on September 1, 2026, aligning closely with the market’s heavy weighting toward these outcomes (combined ~93.5% implied probability).**

Singapore’s equatorial climate produces consistently warm conditions, with afternoon highs typically modulated by humidity, cloud cover, sea breezes, and the south-west monsoon. Current data from August 31 show daytime readings near 29–31°C at Changi Airport and other stations, alongside elevated heat stress indices (WBGT values in the “black” category at multiple sites). Multiple forecasts for September 1 converge on highs of 31–33°C (89–91°F), driven by partly cloudy skies, light southerly winds, and only moderate thunderstorm chances that are unlikely to suppress peak readings significantly. Historical September averages hover near 31°C, but the ongoing El Niño influence and recent trend of more frequent high-heat-stress days have supported slightly elevated expectations. 

Traders appear to be pricing in the consensus range from official and ensemble models while assigning low probability to extremes, reflecting the limited day-to-day variability typical for the region and the absence of major disruptive weather signals in the latest guidance.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for Kuala Lumpur’s highest temperature on September 1, 2026, centers on 34°C (64.5% implied probability) because short-range forecasts from multiple sources converge on an afternoon peak near 34–35°C amid typical convective conditions.**

September marks the start of the inter-monsoon period in the region, when daytime heating drives scattered thunderstorms that frequently limit maximum temperatures despite high solar insolation and urban heat-island effects in the city. Recent August 2026 observations showed above-normal highs (frequently 34–35.7°C), establishing a warm baseline, yet model runs for September 1 consistently incorporate 70–80% storm chances and cloud cover that moderate extremes.

Forecasts illustrate this balance: WeatherBug projects a 94°F (~34.4°C) high with storms, Yr.no shows hourly peaks reaching 35°C before cooling, and other guidance ranges 32–35°C. The strong clustering at 34°C (with 33°C at 24.5%) reflects traders’ assessment that afternoon convection and humidity will prevent both cooler outcomes and the rarer 36°C+ spikes, consistent with climatological September averages of ~32–33°C and low historical probability of sustained extremes under disturbed conditions. Updated model guidance and official observations on September 1 will determine final resolution.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 1 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast consensus for NYC's September 1 high centers on the low-to-mid 80s, aligning with the closely matched market probabilities of 31.5% for 82-83°F and 28.5% for 84-85°F.** Official and ensemble guidance, including National Weather Service-aligned sources, projects a high near 84°F under mostly cloudy skies with a 50% chance of showers and thunderstorms, especially in the afternoon. Southwest winds of 5-10 mph, elevated humidity, and variable cloud cover are key variables that can suppress or allow peaks near the upper end of that range. Afternoon convection introduces timing uncertainty—earlier or heavier rain could cap readings closer to 82°F, while delayed development favors 84-85°F. This setup reflects typical early-September climatology (historical average high ~81°F) with modest warm advection, explaining why lower and higher bins hold far smaller implied probabilities. Updated model runs and radar trends over the next 12-18 hours will likely resolve the narrow spread before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecasts from multiple sources, including WeatherBug, AccuWeather, Yr.no, and the Met Office, indicate a daytime high around 17°C for Buenos Aires on September 1, 2026, under partly cloudy skies with light southerly or easterly winds and minimal precipitation risk.** This places the outcome near the lower end of the distribution, yet market-implied odds favor 20°C (41%) and 21°C (34.5%), with 19°C at 15.5%. Traders appear to price in modest upside from ensemble model spread or localized urban heat effects, while discounting the cooler guidance from operational runs.

Key differentiating factors include the strength and timing of a building high-pressure ridge, which favors diurnal warming through reduced cloud cover and light winds (typically 5–10 km/h), versus any lingering marine influence or slight frontal passage that could cap temperatures. Ensemble members diverge on peak solar heating and boundary-layer mixing; stronger subsidence and clearer skies push maxima toward 20–21°C, while enhanced onshore flow or earlier cloud build-up keeps readings near 17–18°C. Historical early-September climatology (average daily maximum near 18–19°C) and the seasonal transition into spring further support the market’s tilt toward the upper teens, though short-range model consensus currently anchors expectations lower. Upcoming high-resolution model updates and afternoon observations will likely resolve the narrow spread between the leading outcomes.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent cloud cover, widespread showers, and thunderstorms associated with Mexico City's peak rainy season are the dominant factors capping the September 1 maximum near the historical early-September average of roughly 22–23 °C.** Multiple operational forecasts issued August 31 (WeatherBug, Worldmeteo, The Weather Outlook, Yr, and others) converge on a daytime high of 22–24 °C under partly to mostly cloudy skies and 40–95 % rain probability, with peak readings most often expected in the early to mid-afternoon before convective activity intensifies.

The city’s high elevation (~2 240 m) further moderates temperatures, preventing the stronger diurnal rises seen at lower altitudes even on partly sunny days. Recent conditions—ongoing thunderstorms through August 31 and a moist easterly or southerly flow—have kept surface dew points elevated and reduced insolation, reinforcing the expectation that any clearing will be brief and insufficient to push readings much above 25 °C. Model guidance shows limited spread, with only modest upside risk if convection develops later than forecast.

These elements align with the market’s clustering around 23–25 °C, reflecting trader consensus that normal rainy-season dynamics will produce a maximum in that narrow band rather than an outlier warm or cool outcome. Updated model runs and official Servicio Meteorológico Nacional briefings on September 1 morning will provide the final resolution data.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Taipei Songshan Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Taipei Songshan Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/tw/taipei/RCSS.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration and global models indicate a low-pressure system driving unstable conditions and frequent showers or thunderstorms over northern Taiwan through early September, which limits surface heating and caps daily maxima. On September 2 specifically, most guidance shows highs near 29–31 °C (roughly 84–88 °F) amid persistent cloud cover and easterly flow, though brief clearing could allow brief spikes toward 33 °C. Historical early-September baselines average 31–32 °C, but elevated humidity and precipitation probability this week favor the lower end of the distribution. The tight clustering of market-implied odds around 33–35 °C reflects trader weighting of ensemble spread—particularly model divergence on convective timing and any late-day breaks in cloudiness—against the strong baseline signal for suppressed maxima from ongoing moisture. Updated short-range runs and CWA briefings over the next 48 hours will be the key resolution drivers.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent numerical weather model consensus positions 21–22°C as the leading outcomes for Amsterdam’s daily maximum on September 2, 2026.** Official KNMI guidance and multiple ensemble runs (including ECMWF and GFS) currently project a high near 21–22°C under partly cloudy skies with light westerly to southwesterly flow and only limited shower risk. These values sit slightly above the long-term September 2 climatological average of roughly 19–20°C but remain well within normal early-autumn variability for the region.

**Key atmospheric drivers include a transient ridge of high pressure providing modest daytime warming, offset by Atlantic moisture and increasing cloud cover that caps further heating.** Forecast soundings show surface dew points in the mid-teens Celsius and modest lapse rates, limiting the potential for either a sharp spike above 23°C or a drop to 20°C or below. Minor model spread in cloud timing and boundary-layer mixing keeps a small probability on 20°C or 23°C, consistent with the thin market tails.

**No major forecast shifts have occurred in the past 48 hours; the tight clustering around 21–22°C has held steady, which explains why these two outcomes together exceed 89% implied probability.** Traders are effectively pricing the current high-resolution guidance while discounting low-probability outliers, as is typical for short-range temperature markets where model agreement is strong. Updated model runs and KNMI briefings through September 1 will provide the next high-impact data points.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent official forecasts from Argentina’s Servicio Meteorológico Nacional (SMN) for September 2, 2026, in the Buenos Aires area project a maximum of 21°C under mostly cloudy skies, with northwest winds in the morning shifting to northeast and minimal precipitation risk.** This baseline aligns with early-spring climatology, where average September highs typically range 18–22°C as the region transitions from winter. Trader consensus, however, centers on 22–23°C (combined ~70% implied probability), reflecting expectations of modest warming from northerly advection or reduced cloud cover that would enhance daytime solar heating.

Key differentiating factors include short-term model variability in boundary-layer temperatures and wind direction: sustained northerly flow can advect warmer air from the north, potentially pushing peaks 1–2°C above guidance, while persistent cloudiness or a sharper easterly shift would cap readings nearer 21°C. Historical analogs for early September show occasional outliers above 24°C under favorable clear-sky conditions, but current ensemble guidance and the narrow spread between leading outcomes underscore genuine uncertainty around exact maximums within the 21–24°C window. Updated SMN briefings and high-resolution model runs over the next 48 hours remain the primary near-term catalysts.

markets.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=mpmg

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Afternoon thunderstorms, driven by the Intertropical Convergence Zone and warm Caribbean sea-surface temperatures near 29°C, are expected to increase cloud cover and evaporative cooling, capping peaks below the 33°C threshold. Light variable winds and high humidity (70–90%) further limit radiative heating, while the precise timing of showers remains the key variable distinguishing 31°C versus 32°C outcomes. Updated National Meteorological Service of Panama guidance and short-range models over the next 48 hours will clarify whether clearer periods allow brief spikes toward 33°C.
